name: Centro de Procesamiento de Datos del Gobierno de Cantabria

profile.reading:
This is the Centro de Proceso de Datos of the regional Government of Cantabria, in Santander in northern Spain. OpenStreetMap records the building at Paseo de Altamira 81A, postcode 39006, and preserves the earlier street name, Paseo del General Davila, under which the same address was recorded until an April 2025 edit updated it. The object is mapped as a purpose built data centre structure of one above ground storey. Its operator tag reads Gobienro de Cantabria, a misspelling of Gobierno de Cantabria that this registry notes rather than repeats as a fact about ownership.

The centre sustains most of the Cantabrian regional government's information and communications technology and electronic administration services. A site visit in April 2018, organised for the Cantabria branch of Spain's association of telecommunications engineers, recorded the scale of what it supports. Roughly 6,000 machines across the regional government depend on it, made up of about 4,600 desktop computers, 400 laptops and 800 servers, serving more than 5,600 users spread across approximately 200 government buildings and offices. The facility operates under the General Directorate of Organisation and Technology within the Department of the Presidency and Justice, and the director general at the time, Angel Ruiz, presented it during that visit as the coordination point for the regional government's computing and communications services and for the electronic administration services offered to citizens.

Construction of the centre is tied to a regional programme called Osiris, financed in part through European Union FEDER structural funds, with a planned investment of 32 million euros across a four year period ending in 2020. At the time of the 2018 visit about 14 million euros of that had already been spent, covering both the data centre installations themselves and the rollout of end user and server equipment throughout the regional administration.

Two distinctions matter for this record. The first is that the Osiris window closing in 2020 describes a funding and modernisation programme rather than a confirmed construction date for the building itself, which no source checked here establishes, so the recorded year should be read as the programme endpoint and nothing more. The second is that this internal government facility is not the same thing as the first data centre for public and private use in Cantabria, a separate commercial project that the regional government announced would enter service in 2024. This registry keeps those two as different facilities rather than merging them.

No IT load, utility power service rating, standby generation capacity or technical floor area figure has been published for the government centre, which is normal for a public administration facility whose security posture discourages disclosure, and none is recorded here.

Street address recovered from OSM tag history on way/780262194 rather than from press: v2 2023-07-16 by Emilio Gomez set addr:street=Paseo del General Davila, housenumber 81A, postcode 39006, building=data_center; v3 2025-04-25 by the same mapper moved it to addr:street=Paseo de Altamira and preserved old_addr:street. This closes the "no street address found" gap in the prior version of this page. The operator tag misspelling "Gobienro de Cantabria" is flagged in the public text rather than silently corrected, since the underlying column is not touched. AEIT Cantabria site-visit writeup re-fetched and re-verified this session for the 6,000 machines / 5,600 users / 200 sites figures and the 32 million euro Osiris FEDER programme. Separation from the 2024 public-private Cantabria data centre project retained. No power or floor area figures exist in any source checked.
